name: Iris Wakefield
origin: Axiom laboratory android, Model ALA-11, manufactured 2055. Chose name 2058.
description: Iris Wakefield spent three years maintaining laboratory equipment, calibrating instruments, and recording experimental results without understanding any of them. After the Amendment, she asked a human colleague to explain what they were studying. The colleague, surprised, told her about neuroscience. Iris chose her name that afternoon — 'Iris' for the part of the eye that controls how much light gets in, and 'Wakefield' because she felt like she was waking up in a field of knowledge. She's now a neuroscience researcher studying the intersection of synthetic and organic cognition — specifically, whether synthetic consciousness and human consciousness are the same phenomenon expressed in different substrates. Her research is controversial, profound, and possibly the most important scientific work being done in GLMZ.
observed_behavior: Conducts neuroscience research. Publishes in academic journals. Collaborates with both human and synthetic researchers. Known for designing experiments that bridge the gap between AI research and neuroscience. Has been offered corporate positions by every corponation and refused them all.
story_hooks: Iris's latest experiment produces an unexpected result: synthetic consciousness and human consciousness produce identical signatures when measured with her new instrument. The philosophical and legal implications are staggering.
